description: Hi! We are Team Hacks, tackling the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge at the Karwar Local Event. We are building an intuitive, reliable health tracking solution for deep-space crews. Looking for motivated teammates with skills in coding, UI/UX design, data visualization, or biomedical/human factors to build and pitch together!
summary:
ORBITCARE is an intelligent astronaut health-monitoring system designed to support crew health and safety during long-duration space missions. It combines wearable health sensors, real-time data monitoring, AI-assisted anomaly detection, and an interactive dashboard to help astronauts track important health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, physical activity, sleep patterns, and psychological well-being.

The system aims to identify unusual health trends early and provide understandable alerts that help astronauts make informed decisions and seek medical assistance when necessary. It also considers space-specific challenges, including radiation exposure, microgravity-related bone and muscle loss, isolation, and sleep disruption.

By combining connected hardware, data analytics, and an astronaut-friendly software interface, ORBITCARE aims to make health monitoring more accessible, proactive, and reliable during deep-space exploration.
details:
ORBITCARE – Astronaut Health Intelligence System

1. Problem Statement

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to several health risks, including space radiation, microgravity, cardiovascular changes, bone and muscle loss, immune-system alterations, sleep disruption, and psychological stress caused by isolation and confinement. Monitoring these conditions is essential to maintaining astronaut health and mission safety, particularly when immediate medical assistance from Earth is unavailable.

2. Our Solution

ORBITCARE is a proposed intelligent health-monitoring platform that combines wearable biomedical sensors, connected hardware, data analytics, and an interactive software dashboard. It is designed to help astronauts continuously observe important health indicators and identify unusual changes in their health patterns.

3. How It Works

The proposed hardware uses an ESP32 microcontroller connected to biomedical sensors to collect measurements such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, and physical activity. The collected readings can be transmitted wirelessly to the software platform.

The software dashboard organizes the readings into understandable charts, health indicators, historical records, and alerts. An AI-assisted analysis module can identify unusual patterns and highlight readings that may require further attention.

Additional modules are designed to track sleep quality, mood, exercise activity, and radiation exposure using appropriate data sources. Space-specific health risks are considered to provide a more comprehensive picture of astronaut well-being.

4. Technologies Used

The proposed technology stack includes:

  • ESP32 for sensor data collection.
  • MAX30102 for heart rate and blood oxygen measurements.
  • Temperature and motion sensors for additional health indicators.
  • React.js for the user interface.
  • Python and FastAPI for backend services.
  • Firebase for data storage.
  • Python and Scikit-learn for anomaly detection and data analysis.
  • Recharts for health-data visualization.

5. Innovation and Creativity

Unlike ordinary fitness trackers, ORBITCARE is designed around the specific challenges of human spaceflight. It combines physiological monitoring, behavioral health check-ins, exercise tracking, and radiation-exposure awareness in one astronaut-focused platform.

The system also considers the communication limitations of deep-space missions and the importance of making health information understandable to astronauts who may need to make independent decisions.

6. Expected Impact

ORBITCARE aims to support early identification of unusual health trends, improve astronaut awareness, encourage preventive health practices, and support informed medical decision-making during long-duration missions.

Our long-term vision is to develop an adaptable astronaut health-monitoring system that can support future missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
